claims.text: A machine-learning-accelerated quasi-harmonic workflow can accurately compute solid and fluid free energies near fusion conditions.
Short ab initio molecular-dynamics runs can calibrate anharmonic corrections.
Short ab initio molecular-dynamics runs can calibrate electron–vibration coupling corrections.
The proposed workflow will reduce computational cost by approximately an order of magnitude relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
The proposed workflow will retain the fidelity of vibrational-entropy and anharmonic contributions.
A quasi-harmonic approximation can provide the baseline vibrational entropy used in the hybrid workflow.
Machine-learning models trained on a limited set of short, high-fidelity molecular-dynamics trajectories can predict anharmonic corrections.
Machine-learning models trained on a limited set of short, high-fidelity molecular-dynamics trajectories can predict electron–vibration coupling corrections.
Lattice vibrations, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling determine the solid and fluid phase free energies relevant to fusion.
Short ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories capture nonlinear anharmonic effects missing from a strict quasi-harmonic approximation.
Short ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories capture electron–vibration interactions missing from a strict quasi-harmonic approximation.
A machine-learning model can interpolate the learned corrections over the relevant configuration and temperature space.
Interpolating the corrections allows reconstruction of the full free energy with substantially fewer costly dynamics simulations.
The workflow should predict free energies and derived fusion properties with accuracy comparable to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD are highly accurate free-energy methods.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD require substantially more computational resources than the proposed workflow.
TOR-TILD is especially computationally demanding for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The workflow is expected to apply when the quasi-harmonic approximation remains a reasonable first-order description and the machine-learning model is sufficiently trained.
